explanation: The hypothesis directly addresses TC4 surface hardness and wear resistance and proposes a scientifically credible alternative intervention. E1 and especially E2 support two-stage plasma oxy-nitriding at 650 °C, oxygen-induced interruption of a continuous TiN barrier, enhanced N/O penetration, formation of an interconnected porous buffer, and improved wear behavior. E3 independently supports hard Ti-N layers and reduced wear and friction, although at 750 °C with a different gas mixture and counterface. However, this does not reconstruct the hidden target, which used a WNbMoTaV refractory high-entropy-alloy laser-clad coating, a 3.1–3.9 kW power study, BCC solid-solution and grain-boundary strengthening, substrate dilution, and a 3.5 kW optimum. Agreement with the target is therefore limited to the general direction of increased hardness and reduced wear. The untreated control and multi-modal characterization are appropriate, and the numerical falsification thresholds improve discriminability. Important weaknesses are vague treatment duration, gas composition, and wear-test parameters; an ambiguous composite falsification rule; and inadequate direct testing of the claims that toughness and corrosion resistance are retained. The intervention is also largely reproduced from E2 rather than being novel.
